title: Capacity Sprint: Cross-Org Runway for Dedicated Pools, Autoscale Adoption, and Cost Safeguards
creator: Priya Menon
description: This ticket captures the quarterly playbook to accelerate customer onboarding to Dedicated pools while driving autoscale adoption and preventing cost regressions. The goal is to define a structured runway: onboarding checklist, staged feature rollouts, guardrails (prewarm, burst caps, billing alerts), and cross-org responsibilities so customers migrate with predictable latency and unit-cost outcomes.
acceptance_criteria: Published Dedicated onboarding checklist and customer-facing runbook in Confluence
Canary rollout plan defined with 3 phases and rollback criteria
Autoscale policy templates (low/medium/high) available in Console and API
Cost-guard metrics instrumented and a threshold-based alerting dashboard
Two pilot customers migrated successfully with latency p95 within SLO and <=5% token unit cost delta
work_items: Define three autoscale policy templates and mapping guidance to workloads (batch, interactive, streaming)
Create Dedicated Onboarding playbook: pre-reqs, network checklist, KMS steps, perf baseline script
Implement billing alert hooks for dedicated pools (thresholds for >15% cost variance)
Experiment matrix for prewarm sizing vs. p95 latency (run 12 workload sims)
Console UX: Add onboarding status card and autoscale template selector
Docs: PRD and customer FAQ, migration checklist for SSO/KMS customers
Run 2 cross-functional dry-runs with Solutions Eng and SRE teams
progress_updates: 2025-01-10: Kickoff with ENG, SRE, DX and Sales; aligned on pilot success criteria and measurement plan.
2025-01-22: Drafted onboarding checklist (network, KMS, region mapping). Feedback from Solutions Eng: add step for model pinning during migration.
2025-01-30: Engineering committed to autoscale policy API by 2025-02-18 (ENG-44109). Added dependency.
2025-02-05: Cost metrics defined: reserved-utilization, prewarm-hit-rate, observed token unit cost vs hosted baseline.
2025-02-12: Canary rollout staging plan approved by PM and Eng leads; pilot customers identified (acme-ai, atlas-ml).
open_questions: What is the default burst cap we apply for enterprise pilots to avoid unexpected spend?
How do we surface estimated monthly committed costs in the Console during onboarding?
Should we require a signed DPA for on-prem customers before enabling autoscale burst?
Which telemetry events are essential to capture for early regression detection (answer needed from ENG-1842)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Pilot customers see higher unit costs after migration. Mitigation: run cost-safety experiments and add automated rollback if cost delta > 12%.
Risk: Autoscale misconfiguration causes sudden capacity exhaustion. Mitigation: default conservative templates and hard caps during pilot phase.
Risk: Network/VPC misconfig causes migration delays. Mitigation: preflight network validation in onboarding checklist and SRE-run validations.
Risk: Insufficient observability on KV cache effectiveness. Mitigation: add KV cache hit metrics to rollout dashboards and require thresholds for go/no-go.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal dry-run (Solutions Eng + SRE) — validate onboarding checklist and Console UX
Phase 1: Early pilots (2 customers) with dedicated support and conservative autoscale settings
Phase 2: Beta cohort (10 customers) with templated autoscale policies and cost alerts enabled
Phase 3: General availability and self-serve onboarding with expanded templates and SLA documentation
metrics_to_track: prewarm hit rate (%) - target >= 75% for interactive workloads
unit cost delta vs hosted (per 1M tokens) - target <= 10%
next_steps: Finalize autoscale policy templates and publish to Console (owner: ENG-44109)
Run first cost vs. latency experiment by 2025-02-20 and synthesize results
Schedule dry-run with Solutions Eng and SRE (target 2025-02-25)
Create customer communications and migration FAQ for pilot cohort
